title: Learn HTTP Servers in Go
description: Build server-side Go skills with routes, middleware, auth, webhooks, and APIs.

lessons.title: Welcome to Learn HTTP Servers
lessons.instruction: A health endpoint gives operators a cheap readiness signal. Make it answer with the service's ready state.

lessons.title: Goroutines in Servers
lessons.instruction: Go's HTTP server handles requests concurrently, so shared results need coordination. Collect both request results before printing the total.

lessons.title: Project Setup
lessons.instruction: An executable server starts in package main. Choose that package for the entry point.

lessons.title: Server
lessons.instruction: http.ServeMux dispatches requests by registered route patterns. Register the readiness route.

lessons.title: Fileservers
lessons.instruction: http.FileServer maps request paths to files, so an external mount prefix often must be removed. Strip the public prefix before the file handler sees the path.

lessons.title: Fileserver Quiz
lessons.instruction: A missing static file is a missing resource, not a server failure. Select the status it should return.

lessons.title: Serving Images
lessons.instruction: Content-Type tells clients how to interpret response bytes. Send the PNG media type for this image.

lessons.title: Workflow Tips
lessons.instruction: A tight server workflow catches failures before a manual run. Arrange the feedback loop so tests run before the server starts.

lessons.title: Custom Handlers
lessons.instruction: An http.Handler controls status, headers, and body through ResponseWriter. Return a created response from the custom handler.

lessons.title: Handler Review
lessons.instruction: The first body write implicitly sends status 200 unless WriteHeader ran first. Preserve status 202 by writing it before the body.

lessons.title: Middleware
lessons.instruction: Middleware surrounds another handler to add cross-cutting behavior. Add the request marker, then call the wrapped handler.

lessons.title: Stateful Handlers
lessons.instruction: A handler value can retain state between calls. Increment its counter once for each request.

lessons.title: Routing
lessons.instruction: Modern ServeMux patterns can match both an HTTP method and a path. Register a GET route for listing chirps.

lessons.title: Patterns
lessons.instruction: A named ServeMux wildcard captures one path segment for the handler. Read the captured chirp identifier.

lessons.title: Monoliths and Decoupling
lessons.instruction: A narrow interface decouples request logic from a specific storage implementation. Depend on the message store behavior the handler actually uses.

lessons.title: Which Is Better?
lessons.instruction: Service boundaries add operational cost as well as flexibility. Choose the simpler deployment while one team owns one database.

lessons.title: Admin Namespace
lessons.instruction: Administrative endpoints are easier to secure and route under a distinct namespace. Place metrics beneath the admin prefix.

lessons.title: Deployment Options
lessons.instruction: Deployments commonly inject environment configuration at runtime. Read the listening port from that configuration.

lessons.title: HTTP Clients
lessons.instruction: An HTTP client response body owns resources until it is closed. Close it after the server-to-server response is consumed.

lessons.title: JSON
lessons.instruction: JSON struct tags define the wire key independently of the Go field name. Expose Message with the expected key.

lessons.title: JSON Review
lessons.instruction: Malformed JSON is a client input error. Reject a decode failure with bad request instead of continuing with zero values.

lessons.title: The Profane
lessons.instruction: Content filtering should transform only matched tokens. Replace the blocked word while preserving the rest of the chirp.

lessons.title: Storage
lessons.instruction: PostgreSQL is the local persistence service for this course. Run Check to verify that the database accepts a live TCP connection.
lessons.expected: PASS · The live postgres services are ready.

lessons.title: Goose Migrations
lessons.instruction: A migration pairs a forward schema change with a rollback. Order the up and down directions so setup is reversible.

lessons.title: SQLC
lessons.instruction: sqlc turns checked SQL into typed Go methods. Call the generated query method instead of an untyped placeholder.

lessons.title: Database Review
lessons.instruction: A transaction keeps writes provisional until commit. Commit this write so later reads can observe the record.

lessons.title: Context
lessons.instruction: context carries cancellation, deadlines, and request-scoped values across call boundaries. Pass the request identifier through it to the query.

lessons.title: Create User
lessons.instruction: A create endpoint validates input, persists a new resource, then returns its representation. Store the submitted email and return the user.

lessons.title: Create Chirp
lessons.instruction: Ownership must come from authenticated identity rather than a client-supplied user id. Associate the new chirp with that author.

lessons.title: Collections and Singletons
lessons.instruction: Resource-oriented URLs use a collection path for many records and an identifier for one. Complete both chirp paths.

lessons.title: Get All Chirps
lessons.instruction: Stable ordering makes collection responses predictable. Sort stored chirps by identifier before returning them.

lessons.title: Get Chirp
lessons.instruction: A lookup that has no matching resource should return 404. Handle the absent chirp identifier.

lessons.title: Authentication With Passwords
lessons.instruction: Production password storage uses a salted, slow hash such as Argon2id; this small digest fixture only demonstrates not retaining plaintext. Store the derived value.

lessons.title: Password Review
lessons.instruction: Password verification compares a submitted secret with the stored derived value without exposing either one. Complete that comparison.

lessons.title: Types of Authentication
lessons.instruction: Authentication proves identity; common API mechanisms include sessions, keys, and bearer tokens. Use a bearer token for this stateless request.

lessons.title: JWTs
lessons.instruction: A JWT is three base64url segments: header, claims, and signature. Build the token in that order.

lessons.title: Authentication With JWTs
lessons.instruction: The Authorization header carries a scheme followed by credentials. Extract the bearer credential without retaining the scheme.

lessons.title: JWT Review
lessons.instruction: The exp claim limits how long a token is accepted. Reject a token whose expiry precedes the current timestamp.

lessons.title: Revoking JWTs
lessons.instruction: A revocation set invalidates selected tokens before their normal expiry. Reject an identifier found in that set.

lessons.title: Refresh Tokens
lessons.instruction: A short-lived access token can be renewed with a longer-lived refresh token. Rotate the refresh token when it is exchanged.

lessons.title: Cookies
lessons.instruction: The HttpOnly cookie flag prevents client-side scripts from reading a session credential. Enable it here.

lessons.title: Authorization
lessons.instruction: Authorization decides whether an authenticated identity may perform an action. Allow this mutation only for the chirp owner.

lessons.title: Authentication vs. Authorization
lessons.instruction: Authentication identifies the caller; authorization checks permission. Return forbidden when an authenticated caller lacks it.

lessons.title: Delete Chirp
lessons.instruction: A successful deletion can return 204 when no response representation is needed. Delete the owned chirp and use that status.

lessons.title: Webhooks
lessons.instruction: Webhook providers retry deliveries, so processing must be idempotent. Prevent a repeated event from applying its side effect twice.

lessons.title: Webhooks Review
lessons.instruction: Webhook consumers should safely ignore event types they do not handle. Acknowledge this unknown event without applying a side effect.

lessons.title: API Keys
lessons.instruction: Secret comparisons should avoid leaking matching-prefix timing. Compare the supplied API key in constant time.

lessons.title: Documentation
lessons.instruction: Useful API documentation starts with each endpoint's method, path, inputs, and outputs. Describe the chirp collection endpoint's method and path.

lessons.title: Documentation
lessons.instruction: A response contract records both status and representation. Document the created response for the chirp endpoint.

lessons.title: Sorting Chirps
lessons.instruction: Sorting a response should not silently reorder persistent state. Produce descending identifiers without mutating storage.

lessons.title: Adding a README
lessons.instruction: A project README should make the development workflow reproducible. Include setup, migration, test, and run commands.
